sources.title: Randomized controlled trials of aprotinin in cardiac surgery: could clinical equipoise have stopped the bleeding?
sources.version_or_date: Fergusson, Glass, Hutton & Shapiro; Clinical Trials 2005; 2:218–232; DOI 10.1191/1740774505cn085oa
sources.sections_read: pp.218–226: Methods, Results, Discussion, figures1–6 captions (commentary pp.229–232 not counted).
sources.confirmed: 64 trials/8,040 subjects were included; efficacy stabilized by the twelfth trial (June 1992). Prior-trial citation median was 20%; only 15/64 reported enrolment dates, and publication dates with a one-year allowance were used. The study tested transfusion efficacy, not whether safety research could stop.
sources.limits: Missing citation is not direct evidence of ignorance; retrospective threshold and publication lag limit preventable-cost attribution. Authors explicitly leave serious adverse outcomes unsettled.
sources.observation_window_note: The abstract reports 1987–2002 for included trials. Methods describe updated searches through 2004; trial publication and enrolment dates must not be conflated.
sources.additional_checks: p.222 reports actual simple PubMed searches: aprotinin + RCT publication filter retrieved 58/62 publications; aprotinin AND random* retrieved 51/62. This is the paper authors’ retrospective search, not a present software baseline.

sources.title: Avoidable waste in the production and reporting of research evidence
sources.sections_read: Uploaded original Lancet body: pp.86–88 intro, four-stage figure, unnecessary/poorly designed studies, reporting, conclusions.
sources.confirmed: The >85% estimate compounds approximately 50% losses at three stages, conditional on heterogeneous evidence generalizing. Existing-evidence ignorance is only one component; the authors also identify wrong questions, biased design, nonpublication and unusable reporting.
sources.limits: This is a viewpoint synthesis, not a cohort estimate of duplicate-trial prevalence. ResearchGate header describes a later reprint, while the uploaded text is the dated Lancet original; do not equate >85% with avoidable software-reinvention cost.

sources.title: Hindsight Bias
sources.version_or_date: Roese & Vohs 2012; Perspectives on Psychological Science 7(5):411–426; DOI 10.1177/1745691612454303
sources.sections_read: pp.411–413; three-level framework; Debiasing Hindsight Bias; discussion.
sources.confirmed: The review distinguishes memory distortion, inevitability, and foreseeability, with cognitive, metacognitive and motivational inputs. Considering alternative outcomes can reduce bias, but difficult alternative-generation tasks can reverse that effect.
sources.limits: Review of experiments, not a frequency estimate for retrospective software narratives. Knowing an alternative existed does not establish that the original team should have predicted its later success.

sources.title: How Reuse Influences Productivity in Object-Oriented Systems
sources.version_or_date: Basili, Briand & Melo 1996; CACM 39(10):104–116; empirical observation Sep–Dec1994
sources.sections_read: pp.104–105 participants; p.109Validity; pp.112–114 reuse/error density and rework.
sources.confirmed: Eight teams of three graduate students developed comparable small C++ systems. Reuse rates 0–64% were associated with fewer defects and less rework; rework was measured by error-repair effort, including understanding, locating, checking consequences, implementing and regression testing.
sources.limits: Reuse levels were not randomized. Small educational systems, single application domain and preexisting libraries limit external validity; the study does not measure initially missed alternatives or counterfactual wasted effort.

sources.title: License Risks from Ad Hoc Reuse of Code from the Internet
sources.sections_read: pp.76–79 survey, reuse extent, regression, information sources; p.81 validity/conclusion.
sources.confirmed: Survey of 869 current/former professional developers; current-worker descriptive figures use N=732 and regression N=807. Internet 65% and friends/colleagues 46% were reported learning channels among 732; 59% rated ad-hoc reuse at least somewhat important.
sources.limits: Self-selected newsgroup survey with 9.9% response rate; importance and channel measures are self-reports. License knowledge and suitability can make rejection of discovered code rational; no measured reinvention loss.

sources.title: Managing Incidents
sources.version_or_date: Andrew Stribblehill; edited Kavita Guliani; Site Reliability Engineering 2016; live chapter
sources.sections_read: chapter14 opening, Elements of Incident Management Process, The Role of Incident Commander, A Recognized Command Post, Clear Live Incident State Document, Explicit Handoff.
sources.confirmed: The practitioner chapter explicitly bases Google's incident management on Incident Command System. It specifies commander/operations/communications/planning roles, restricting changes to operations, live state, command posts and explicit handoff.
sources.limits: This documents real structural borrowing by publication 2016; earliest internal adoption date and any late-discovery cost are not stated. The Mary scenario is hypothetical and is not an observed outage.

sources.title: Innovation at Mettle – Double-Entry and Event-Sourcing
sources.sections_read: body: accounting experience; event sourcing relation; WODE schema and balances; immutable ledger.
sources.confirmed: Mettle describes recognizing how accountants' double-entry methods relate to event sourcing and implements WODE with timestamp/source/destination/amount so transfers preserve a balance. Appended events cannot be edited or deleted.
sources.limits: Actual structural transfer is documented, but accounting is the bank's business domain, so distance is limited. First adoption/decision dates, rejected old implementation and saved cost are absent; this is not a late-discovery case.

sources.title: Circuit Breaker
sources.version_or_date: Martin Fowler2014-03-06
sources.sections_read: body and Ruby example; self-reset/half-open; synchronous/asynchronous discussion.
sources.confirmed: The article credits Michael Nygard with popularizing the pattern and provides executable-style wrapper logic with failure thresholds, opening and recovery tests. The physical protection analogy corresponds to actual control flow rather than a decorative name.
sources.limits: This primary 2014 explanation is not proof of first invention or that Nygard discovered electrical breakers late. Software half-open/retry behavior differs from simple physical manual reset; no migration cost observed.

sources.title: Reactive Streams
sources.version_or_date: Live official specification overview; JVM 1.0.4 release 2022-05-26
sources.sections_read: complete 69-line page: problem statement, goals, JVM standard andJava 9 Flow relation.
sources.confirmed: The specification requires nonblocking backpressure across asynchronous boundaries to keep intermediary queues bounded. It explicitly addresses protocol semantics, not the physical-fluid historical origin often inferred from the name.
sources.limits: The official overview does not document cross-field discovery or initial date of borrowing. Mechanism is real but a fluid-mechanics lineage is unverified; no late-discovery incident is claimed.
sources.cross_check: M28 distinguishes differential-backlog routing from other backpressure meanings. Do not infer a fluid-dynamics historical lineage for Reactive Streams from the name.

sources.title: Success and Failure Factors in Software Reuse
sources.version_or_date: Morisio, Ezran & Tully 2002; IEEE TSE 28(4):340–357; DOI 10.1109/TSE.2002.995420; author manuscript
sources.sections_read: §2 Research approach; §5.1 success/failure and setup for failure analysis; original author manuscript.
sources.confirmed: 19 structured interviews covered 24 reuse-introduction projects from 1994–1997 in 19 European companies; the candidate funnel was 288→62→32→24. Repositories alone were insufficient: management commitment, changed development processes and human factors separated successes from failures.
sources.limits: Retrospective selected improvement projects, qualitative postformed codes and small sample cannot establish software-wide failure frequency or ignorance-caused costs.

sources.title: Code Reuse in Open Source Software Development: Quantitative Evidence, Drivers, and Impediments
sources.sections_read: Original text§4 data; §5.1 importance; §5.2 benefits/issues; §5.3 regression; §5.4 validity.
sources.confirmed: 686 OSS developers responded; key complete-case descriptive tables use N=624, with reported reused-functionality mean 30% and median 20%. Personal networks/project experience support local-search access; loss of control, dependencies and update integration are stated drawbacks.
sources.limits: Self-reported cross-sectional associations; neither code traces nor causal estimates of an alternative-finding product. Challenge-seeking relates to observed reuse but fun alone is not a confirmed deterrent.

sources.title: Accumulating Research: A Systematic Account of How Cumulative Meta-Analyses Would Have Provided Knowledge, Improved Health, Reduced Harm and Saved Resources
sources.version_or_date: Clarke, Brice & Chalmers 2014-07-28; PLOS ONE 9(7):e102670
sources.sections_read: Methods/inclusion/search/assessment; Results four trajectory types; Discussion.
sources.confirmed: June 2012 searches identified 50 eligible reports published 1992–2012 containing >1,500 cumulative meta-analyses. The paper includes stable effects, reversal of early favorable/unfavorable results and later trials too small to resolve uncertainty.
sources.limits: A selected collection of cumulative analyses is not a representative trial-duplication denominator. Repeated work may correct early error or address unresolved endpoints; retrospective stopping thresholds require care.

sources.title: Empirical Evidence on the Validity of Litigated Patents
sources.version_or_date: Allison & Lemley 1998; AIPLA QJ 26:185–275; original issue scan
sources.sections_read: pp.194–205 population, coding, limitations; pp.205–207 validity; pp.231–234 cited versus uncited prior art and footnotes.
sources.confirmed: The population is 299 patents in 239 reported final-validity cases (1989–1996); one split decision yields 300 outcomes, of which 138 (46%) are invalid. Prior-art tests cover 202 patents and 267 cited/uncited-art observations (overlap allowed): invalidity rates 40.8% versus 29.6%, p=.057, so the comparison does not meet a 95% significance threshold.
sources.limits: Invalidity is not synonymous with newly discovered prior art. These selected final cases exclude settlements/nonfinal decisions and cannot estimate all granted patents or the applicant's original awareness.

sources.title: Ex Parte Reexamination Filing Data
sources.version_or_date: USPTO; first report through 2025-09-30;18-page historical bundle
sources.sections_read: First 2 pages: request counts, pendency, certificate outcomes and footnotes.
sources.confirmed: 1981-07-01 to 2025-09-30: 16,022 requests and 13,126 certificates. 1,898/13126(14.5%)all requested claims canceled, 8,309(63.3%)changed, 2,919(22.2%)confirmed; mean/median filing-to-certificate pendency 25.2/18.9 months.
sources.limits: Certificates, requests, patents and claims are distinct units. Requested claims only; merged reexaminations counted once. This selected process measures revision and duration, not ignorance prevalence or litigants' monetary loss.
authors: United States Patent and Trademark Office

sources.title: Applicant and Examiner Citations in US Patents: An Overview and Analysis
sources.version_or_date: Alcácer, Gittelman & Sampat; July 2008 working paper09-016 (not later 2009 journal version)
sources.sections_read: §1 citation interpretation; §4 data/variables; Table 1 and accompanying interpretation (not all regression sections).
sources.confirmed: 502,390 US utility patents issued 2001-01-01 through 2003-12-31 separate applicant and examiner references. Mean patent-level examiner share 63%, while pooled citation-dyad share 41%; about 40% of patents have all citations supplied by examiners.
sources.limits: Examiner-origin references do not show the inventor lacked knowledge. Applicant references can include foreign-office search reports; strategic disclosure and institutional practices confound a knowledge-flow interpretation.

sources.title: Singletons and Multiples in Scientific Discovery: A Chapter in the Sociology of Science
sources.version_or_date: Robert K. Merton 1961-10-13; Proc. APS 105(5):470–486; presented 1961-01-23
sources.sections_read: pp.474–481 adumbrationism, rediscovery/unpublished prior work and priority; pp.483–486 264 multiples and qualifications.
sources.confirmed: Merton and Barber's provisional collection contains 264 multiples: 179 doublets, 51 triplets, 17 quadruplets, 6 quintuplets, 8 sextuplets, 1 septuplet, 2 nonaries. Cases are coded by discipline, timing, priority disputes and participants; unpublished antecedents cannot be assumed discoverable.
sources.limits: The denominator is selected multiples, not all discoveries. The paper rejects reading vague old ideas as exact anticipations and treats independence and chronological simultaneity separately; no wasted-cost estimate.

sources.title: A Brief History of Kanban for Knowledge Work
sources.version_or_date: David J. Anderson; live retrospective article (publication date not shown); internal events October 2004, winter 2005, September 2006, January 2007
sources.sections_read: timeline October 2004 through2007; origin distinction DBR→kanban; board introduction.
sources.confirmed: Anderson says the 2004 Microsoft pull system originated in Theory of Constraints drum-buffer-rope; Don Reinertsen persuaded him toward kanban in winter 2005, changing little beyond possible WIP limits. A physical Corbis board followed in January 2007.
sources.limits: First-person origin account is commercially interested and retrospective, not independent priority proof. It contradicts a simple 'board copied from Toyota in 2004' story; no late-discovery loss demonstrated.
sources.cross_check: M27 original 2010 book adds preexisting awareness and unchanged-Microsoft-outcome counterexample; different narrative dates must be retained.

sources.title: The Hindsight Bias: A Meta-analysis
sources.version_or_date: Christensen-Szalanski & Willham 1991; OBHDP 48:147–168; DOI 10.1016/0749-5978(91)90010-Q
sources.sections_read: pp.149–150 selection; Table 1 p.155; pp.158–160 practical decision effects.
sources.confirmed: 122 studies / 7,359 participants yield sample-weighted uncorrected r=.17; task familiarity and positive/negative outcome information moderate effects. The review separates probability shifts, statistical significance and whether a decision threshold is crossed.
sources.limits: Searches ended July 1989; old task set does not estimate today's software-author bias. Small average effects can matter near a threshold, and a documented bias does not invalidate every retrospective account.

sources.title: Large-scale Code Reuse in Open Source Software
sources.version_or_date: Audris Mockus; ICSE'07 FLOSS workshop 2007-05-21; author PDF
sources.sections_read: §3 sampling/directorymatching; §4 results; §5 threats; §6 discussion.
sources.confirmed: 13.2 million files from49.9 thousand bundles canonicalized to 38.7 thousand projects; 5.3 million text-file paths formed the comparison universe. About half were used across projects; repeated common filenames were excluded and >5 shared files plus overlap thresholds identified candidate components.
sources.limits: Copied-code detection misses renamed code and separately retrieved dependencies. Duplication here is evidence of reuse, not evidence of reinvention or avoidable engineering work; no cost attribution.

sources.title: Self-Nonself Discrimination in a Computer
sources.version_or_date: Forrest, Perelson, Allen & Cherukuri 1994; IEEE Symposium on Research in Security and Privacy:202–212
sources.sections_read: §1 intro/systemoverview; §3 experiments; §4 discussion.
sources.confirmed: The authors explicitly adapt T-cell negative selection into detector-generation and monitoring phases. They test random strings, compiled SPARC instructions and DOS COM virus files; the paper calls practical deployment an open problem.
sources.limits: This is actual algorithmic borrowing from immunology, not only the word 'virus'. Preliminary experiments do not establish production utility or the frequency/cost of teams discovering immunology late.

sources.title: Epidemic Algorithms for Replicated Database Maintenance
sources.version_or_date: PODC 1987; DOI 10.1145/41840.41841; 1987 ACM copyright and /87/0008 code directly visible in Cornell copy.
sources.sections_read: Introduction; §0.1 Motivation; anti-entropy and rumor-mongering mechanisms; spatial distribution counterexamples; conclusion. Cornell copy cover/date and pp.1–2 rechecked.
sources.confirmed: The authors apply epidemic mathematics to randomized replication; anti-entropy was installed in Xerox Clearinghouse. The early-1986 problem investigation found excessive remailing in a system already using anti-entropy; disabling remailing alone was insufficient.
sources.limits: The mathematical mechanism and deployment are explicit, but the account does not say epidemiology was previously unknown. Its 300-site/90,000-message example is illustrative, not an observed incident count or measured migration cost.

sources.title: The Operational Analysis of Queueing Network Models
sources.version_or_date: Denning & Buzen 1978-09; ACM Computing Surveys 10(3):225–261
sources.sections_read: Introduction; operationalvariables/laws; Little's Law p.235; response-time formulas pp.237–238.
sources.confirmed: The authors derive computer-system queueing relations from measurable finite-window quantities, including Little's Law and flow-balance conditions. Their history identifies Scherr's 1965 CTSS application of the machine-repairman model.
sources.limits: This directly documents computer performance use and assumptions, but the Scherr 1965 firstness statement is retrospective unless his original record is opened. Queueing average identities do not by themselves guarantee lower latency or justify arbitrary WIP cuts.

sources.title: Optimization by Simulated Annealing
sources.version_or_date: Kirkpatrick, Gelatt & Vecchi; Science 220(4598):671–680; 1983-05-13; DOI 10.1126/science.220.4598.671
sources.sections_read: pp.671–672 statistical-mechanics mapping; p.679 summary and conclusions; examples of placement and routing inspected.
sources.confirmed: The original authors map energy to optimization cost and physical temperature to a search parameter, using Metropolis acceptance to permit uphill moves. Their four required ingredients are configuration, move generator, objective function and annealing schedule.
sources.limits: Actual algorithmic transfer is explicit; finite schedule performance remains problem dependent and move/objective design needs domain insight. This paper is not a measured late-discovery cost case or proof of global invention priority.

sources.title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
sources.version_or_date: John D. C. Little 1961; Operations Research 9(3):383–387; received 1960-11-09; DOI 10.1287/opre.9.3.383
sources.sections_read: Complete original pp.383–387: definitions, Theorems 1–2, proof, discussion.
sources.confirmed: Little proves the average-number/arrival-rate/wait relation under explicit stationarity, finite-mean and ergodic assumptions, and requires consistent system boundaries. The discussion gives a counterexample when arrival rate includes customers who do not join.
sources.limits: A mathematical identity is not evidence that changing one term leaves the others fixed. This is an original queueing proof, not the first software adoption; M22 documents computer application.

sources.title: Bridging Academia and Industry: How Geographic Hubs Connect University Science and Corporate Technology
sources.version_or_date: Bikard & Marx; online 2019-09-23; Management Science 66(8):3425–3443(2020); DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2019.3385
sources.sections_read: §3 twin-identification and patent-citation analysis; discussion and limitations; original author-licensed full text.
sources.confirmed: A 2000–2010 corpus of 42,106 articles in 15 journals generated 720 paper pairs / 1,246 papers / 578 discoveries; final citation analysis uses 147 discoveries embodied in 316 papers, 697 patents and 1,671 paper-patent dyads. Same-discovery comparisons help hold content constant when measuring unequal industrial attention.
sources.limits: Co-citation screening favors visible discoveries and citation is an attention proxy. Authors cannot distinguish active monitoring from passive exposure or show that attention to hubs improves innovation; none of these denominators measures avoidable duplicate work.

sources.title: Little’s Law as Viewed on Its 50th Anniversary
sources.version_or_date: John D. C. Little 2011; Operations Research 59(3):536–549; DOI 10.1287/opre.1110.0940; authorized reprint 2016-12-18
sources.sections_read: §1–2 finite-window formulation; §4.1 computerarchitecture; §5 first-person history.
sources.confirmed: Little connects queueing measures to requests, throughput and latency, and explains finite-window conditions needed in practice. His own history traces the general-proof question to teaching with Morse 1958 and a student's challenge, rather than a late software-team discovery.
sources.limits: Retrospective origin history and selected applications do not establish a universal adoption path. Operational identities can diagnose coupled measures but do not tell a manager which intervention will fix the system.

sources.title: Kanban: Successful Evolutionary Change for Your Technology Business
sources.version_or_date: David J. Anderson; Blue Hole Press 2010; ISBN 978-0-9845214-1-8 (PDF)
sources.sections_read: Copyright p.iv; Reinertsen foreword pp.xiii–xiv; chapter 1 pp.4–6; chapter 2 pp.11–12. Other chapters not counted.
sources.confirmed: Anderson says he knew the kanban mechanism but doubted its usefulness for knowledge work and did not know its continuous-improvement role. He also says the final Microsoft outcome would have been identical had it been conceived as kanban from the start; this limits the benefit attributable to earlier recognition.
sources.limits: The foreword dates Reinertsen's visit to March 2005; chapter 1 narrative order references winter-2006 presentations before the visit; chapter 2 dates a separate park-card realization to 2005-04-09. Keep these awareness events separate. No measured late-discovery cost. Excluded from method minimum as a candidate event/counterexample record.

sources.title: Notes on Backpressure Routing
sources.version_or_date: Michael J. Neely; EE 649 Stochastic Network Optimization; Spring 2011
sources.sections_read: §I history and pressure-gradient analogy; §II model assumptions; §III Lyapunov drift and B delay caveat; §IV extensions; references.
sources.confirmed: Neely distinguishes earlier window flow control from the later name for max-weight/differential-backlog routing, linking the latter to his own 2003 thesis and 2005 coauthored paper. A real pressure-gradient mapping and Lyapunov mechanism are explained, but throughput stability can coexist with arbitrarily bad packet delay.
sources.limits: Author's technical exposition is primary for his framing, not direct inspection of every cited predecessor. Shared terminology does not establish that Reactive Streams uses this routing algorithm or that engineers discovered fluid dynamics late.
